# Intake Brief: Plan/intake skills iterate over children & verify AC coverage

## Problem statement

When the `plan` or `intake` skills run on a work item that has child work items,
they currently process only the target item — they never descend into the
children. This leaves parent/child AC coverage unverified: a parent's acceptance
criteria may not be collectively covered by its children's ACs, and children are
never themselves planned/intaked (so the decomposition tree can be incomplete
or inconsistent at depth).

## Users

- **Agents running `/skill:plan`** on an epic or other parent with children —
  need the skill to recurse over the whole tree so every level is planned, and
  to verify that the union of child ACs covers the parent ACs.
- **Agents running `/skill:intake`** on a parent with children — need intake to
  run per child (when children exist) and to verify cross-level AC coverage.
- **Operators** — get decomposition trees whose ACs are guaranteed (or
  explicitly flagged) to cover their parents, with gaps auto-closed where
  resolvable and hard conflicts surfaced instead of silently passing.

Example user stories:

- As an agent planning an epic with children, I want the plan skill to iterate
  the whole subtree (respecting dependency order) so I don't have to invoke
  `/skill:plan` per child manually.
- As an agent planning a parent, I want a final review step that verifies the
  children's ACs collectively cover the parent's ACs, auto-closing gaps it can
  resolve and stopping with a clear report when it cannot, so a `plan_complete`
  stage is only reached when coverage is guaranteed.
- As an operator re-running intake on a decomposed epic, I want intake to verify
  AC coverage across the existing children (and per child when configured) so
  the tree stays coherent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (tree iteration — plan):** Running `/skill:plan` on a work item with
  children processes the entire subtree, not just the target: the skill
  iterates children (each child's own plan run, recursing to any depth), in
  dependency order first (`wl dep` edges), then listed order. Verified by a
  test with a multi-level tree (parent → children → grandchildren) asserting
  every node is planned and the processing order respects `wl dep` edges.
- **AC2 (tree iteration — intake):** Running `/skill:intake` on a work item
  with children runs intake per child (recursing the subtree) and also verifies
  AC coverage across existing children. Verified by a test where intake on a
  parent with children runs per child and reports coverage.
- **AC3 (collective coverage):** After processing, for every parent node in the
  tree, the union of its children's acceptance criteria collectively covers the
  parent's acceptance criteria (each parent AC is covered by at least one child
  AC). Verified by a coverage-check test with a parent whose ACs are covered
  by children and a negative test where coverage is missing.
- **AC4 (final review step — auto-close & stop):** The skills' final review
  step closes coverage gaps it can resolve unambiguously (e.g. adding a missing
  child AC that directly maps to an uncovered parent AC), and when a gap or
  conflict cannot be resolved, stops and reports rather than advancing
  (`plan_complete`/`intake_complete` not set; item left `open` with a comment
  describing the conflict). Verified by tests: one where an unambiguous gap is
  auto-closed, one where an unresolvable conflict prevents stage advancement.
- **AC5 (docs & tests):** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
  changes (plan SKILL.md, intake SKILL.md, shared helper docstrings), and the
  full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Worklog API only:** read children via `wl show <id> --children --json`;
  dependency edges via `wl dep list <id> --json`. No direct worklog file edits.
- **No work item for the process itself:** the skills must not create a work
  item to track the iteration itself.
- **Idempotence:** re-running must not create duplicate children or duplicate
  comments; existing children are reused/updated per the existing plan-skill
  idempotence rules.
- **Status lifecycle:** all status transitions go through `StatusLifecycle`
  (intake via `intake.py`, plan via `StatusLifecycle.update_status`); the new
  final review step must leave the item in a valid terminal status (`open`,
  `blocked`, or `completed`) even when it stops on an unresolvable conflict.
- **Conservative auto-closing:** only close gaps that are unambiguous (a child
  AC that clearly maps to an uncovered parent AC). Never invent requirements —
  if intent is unclear, record an Open Question / stop instead.
- **Scope:** affects the `plan` and `intake` skills (SKILL.md workflows) and
  their shared helpers. Must not change audit, implement, or other skills'
  behavior. Must not alter the audit skill's parent-child verdict semantics.

## Existing state

- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` decomposes the target into child feature work items;
  it creates children (Process step 7) and runs six automated review stages on
  the freshly generated feature plan, but never recurses into children and has
  no AC-coverage check across the tree. Its "Automated review on existing
  content" path (skip decision) reviews existing content but still does not
  iterate the tree.
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` prepares a single work item (claim → gather → draft →
  five mini-reviews → find-related → finish). It has no child iteration or
  coverage verification.
- `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` provides shared autoplan/approval-gate logic;
  it has no tree/coverage helpers.
- `wl` supports `wl show <id> --children --json` and `wl dep list/add/rm`, so
  tree traversal and ordering data are available without new CLI work.
- The audit skill already has parent/child awareness (child stage checks,
  inherited passes) — a useful reference for tree semantics but NOT to be
  modified by this item.

## Desired change

- **Shared helper (new or extended):** a module (e.g.
  `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` or new functions in `plan_helpers.py`) that:
  1. Fetches the full descendant tree via `wl show <id> --children --json`.
  2. Orders siblings by `wl dep` edges (topological) then listed order.
  3. Extracts ACs from each item's description (`## Acceptance Criteria`
     section).
  4. Computes coverage: for each parent AC, whether any child AC covers it.
  5. Auto-closes unambiguous gaps; returns an explicit list of unresolvable
     conflicts.
- **Plan skill:** add a "tree iteration" step (before/around Process step 7)
  that recurses into children; add a final "AC coverage review" step after the
  six review stages that applies the helper, auto-closes gaps, and on
  unresolvable conflicts stops without advancing the stage (leaving the item
  `open` with a conflict comment).
- **Intake skill:** add a per-child intake pass (when children exist) and a
  final AC-coverage verification step mirroring the plan behavior.
- **Tests:** unit tests for the shared helper (tree fetch/order, AC extraction,
  coverage computation, gap auto-close, conflict detection) plus skill-workflow
  tests asserting stage advancement is blocked on unresolvable conflicts.

## Key Files

- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — Add tree-iteration and final AC-coverage review steps
  to the Process section.
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — Add per-child intake pass and AC-coverage
  verification step.
- `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` (new) — Shared tree traversal, ordering,
  AC extraction, coverage computation, gap auto-close, conflict detection
  (or equivalent functions added to `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` if shared
  placement is not preferred).
- `skill/plan/tests/test_plan_helpers.py` — Extend with tree/coverage helper
  tests (or add `skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py`).
- `skill/intake/tests/` — Workflow tests for per-child intake and coverage
  stop/advance behavior.

## Related work

- `SA-0MRW0G0XZ009TU6E` — Audit runner circular dependency fix; documents the
  audit skill's child-stage semantics (children in `in_review` don't block
  parent closure). Reference only; not to be modified here.
- `SA-0MSK9IOEF007PP5S` — Audit skill: reduce wall-clock time; example of a
  parent item decomposed into children via the plan skill.
- `SA-0MSJI53RX006E2PS` — Reduce initial LLM context; an epic with 6 children,
  useful as a real-world tree for manual validation of the new iteration.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — Already has child-aware logic (recursive child
  implementations, terminal-stage checks); a pattern reference for how skills
  handle trees.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` + `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Parent/child
  verdict and stage semantics; reference for tree behavior conventions.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: recursion depth/time.** Deep trees could make plan/intake slow or
  loop. Mitigation: recursion bounded by the actual tree; each child processed
  once; idempotent re-runs. Note: no explicit depth cap is assumed unless
  needed — flag in implementation if cycles are possible in worklog trees.
- **Risk: AC extraction brittleness.** Descriptions vary in formatting; ACs may
  be missing or malformed. Mitigation: tolerant extraction; missing ACs treated
  as an uncovered gap reported to the user rather than silently ignored.
- **Risk: auto-closing gaps could invent content.** Mitigation: only
  unambiguous, directly-mapped gaps are auto-closed; everything else stops with
  a report (per AC4).
- **Assumption:** worklog trees are acyclic (a work item's children cannot
  contain it). If a cycle is ever detected, the skill stops and reports.
- **Assumption:** `wl dep list <id> --json` output shape is stable; the helper
  parses both object and array JSON shapes (per existing plan skill guidance).
- **Scope-creep note:** any additional "verify child ACs against parent at
  audit time" ideas are out of scope for this item (audit behavior unchanged)
  and would be tracked as separate work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should the iteration recurse through the entire tree (a parent with
  children whose children also have children — plan/intake each level), or just
  one level of direct children?" — Answer (user): "entire tree". Final: entire
  tree, any depth.
- Q2: "Does 'run the skill on each dependently' mean respecting the `wl dep`
  dependency edges (topological order — an item only after its prerequisites)?
  Or just sequential order as listed?" — Answer (user): "respect dependencies,
  then order listed". Final: topological order by `wl dep` edges, ties broken
  by listed order.
- Q3: "When the final review finds parent ACs not covered by child ACs, should
  the skill block completion (refuse to advance to `plan_complete`/`intake_complete`
  until fixed or explicitly waived), or report the gaps and continue?" — Answer
  (user): "it should close the gaps. If there is conflict that cannot be
  resolved then stop and report, refusing to advance". Final: auto-close
  unambiguous gaps; unresolvable conflicts stop the skill, item left `open`
  with a report comment, stage not advanced.
- Q4: "When intake runs on a parent with children (e.g. re-running on a
  decomposed epic), should it: (a) run intake per child, (b) only verify AC
  coverage across existing children, or (c) both?" — Answer (user): "both".
  Final: intake runs per child AND verifies coverage across existing children.

Source: interactive replies from operator, session 019fe678-68d1-7c92-8723-aeab0ba45cd8.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MRGKZ3QY003498O** – Intake and plan skills should not require CHANGELOG.md updates — handled by ship skill (completed)
- **SA-0MSAIY59V001KECF** – Phase 2: batch child deep analysis into parent call (P6, optional later) (completed)
- **SA-0MS4NWUQC003HWCI** – [MEDIUM] skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py:2019 — Unpacked variable `child_report` is never used (RUF059) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-child-iteration-SA-0MSLRVQIF0040GAM.md` — matched: acceptance, acs, child, children, collectively, cover, coverage, criteria, dependency, dependently, final, intake, item, iterate, one, order, over, parent, plan, respecting, review, run, running, should, skill, skills, step, when, work
- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` — matched: acceptance, acs, child, children, cover, coverage, criteria, dependency, dependently, ensure, intake, item, medium, one, order, over, parent, plan, priority, respecting, review, run, should, skill, skills, step, when, work
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: acceptance, acs, child, children, cover, criteria, dependently, ensure, final, holds, intake, item, medium, one, order, over, parent, plan, priority, review, run, running, should, skill, skills, step, when, work

## Problem

A docs-only reorg of `skill/implement/SKILL.md` was prepared but never committed (stashed as `stash@{0}` — 'uncommitted implement SKILL.md reorg (blocking release)'). The release required a clean tree and the change had no work item, so it was stashed and left undecided. This work item tracks applying it.

## Summary of the change

1. **Move error/abort handling to the top** — new standalone 'Error/exception handling (abort on unexpected errors)' and 'User-initiated abort' sections placed after 'Handling Assets', previously buried at the end of Step 5.
2. **Claim step now assigns the agent** — Step 1 uses `StatusLifecycle.update_status(<id>, "in_progress", stage="in_progress", assignee="<AGENT>")`; duplicate claim instruction removed from Step 3.
3. **Renumber steps correctly** — old doc had 5 → 7 (refactor) → 6 (self-review) → 8 (commit); new order is 5 → 6 (Automated self-review) → 7 (refactor) → 8 (commit/push/in_review).
4. **Remove 'Wait for user confirmation before proceeding.'** from end of Step 5.
5. **Remove stale line** — 'Check for a recent audit record; if none, run /skill:audit' (audit handled in step 6).
6. **Sharpen pre-push discipline** — run full test suite via /skill:test and fix failures; invoke triage helper only for out-of-scope failures.
7. **Fix references** — 'not at Step 7' → 'not at Step 8'; StatusLifecycle table updated to match new step numbers.

Stash base f106f807 is an ancestor of dev and skill/implement/SKILL.md is unchanged between base and dev, so the stash applies cleanly.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `skill/implement/SKILL.md` contains all seven changes above (verified by diff against the stash content).
2. The worktree tree is clean and only `skill/implement/SKILL.md` is modified.
3. Full project test suite passes (node + pytest), build order: build → test → commit.
4. Committed to dev with the change associated with this work item; commit hash recorded in a work item comment.
5. Stash@{0} removed (or verified consumed) after application.

# All skills emit `</end_session>` marker on terminal state

## Problem statement

Skills currently end sessions with inconsistent closing text — some print `<work-item-id>: <summary>`, others say "This completes the <skill> process for <id>", and others produce varied output. A standardized `</end_session>` marker at the very end of every terminal skill session would make it easy for both humans and automation to detect session completion.

## Users

- **Operators (producers)** scanning session output who need a reliable visual cue that a skill has finished without pending questions.
- **Automation loops** (e.g., Ralph) that invoke skills programmatically and need a deterministic signal to detect when a skill has reached a terminal state.

### User stories

- As an operator, I want to see `</end_session>` as the last line of every skill session, so I can instantly know the skill has completed.
- As an automation system, I want to grep for `</end_session>` in a skill's output to reliably detect completion, so I don't have to parse unpredictable closing text.
- As a skill author, I want a single sentence to add as my skill's final step, so I don't have to invent my own closing convention.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A single sentence is added as the final step to **every** work-item workflow skill in `skill/*/SKILL.md` (intake, plan, implement, audit, refactor, cleanup, ship, triage, test, effort-and-risk, find-related, code-review, resolve-pr-comments, author-command) and the report helper (`skill/report/SKILL.md` / `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py`) instructing the agent to end its terminal output with `</end_session>` on its own line. `skill/git-management` and `skill/owner-inference` are excluded — deleted in SA-0MSN81W9G006K0K8.
- [ ] The `</end_session>` marker is **not** added to helper-only skills that don't have their own session lifecycle (e.g., `speak`).
- [ ] The marker is emitted **only** when the skill reaches a terminal state without open questions for the operator — question-ended sessions (where the agent is asking for clarification) do not output the marker.
- [ ] The standardized report helper skill (SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S children: SA-0MSRFPUTN0089F3U, SA-0MSRFTP2Y008BH6L, SA-0MSRFTUGH002IZE4, SA-0MSRFTYOI000W0IQ) includes `</end_session>` as its final output line when producing a report, since it is invoked by the work-item skills.
- [ ] The existing closing conventions (e.g., implement's `<work-item-id>: <summary> / Work committed to dev`, intake's "This completes the Intake process…") are preserved **before** `</end_session>` — the marker is appended, not a replacement.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Scope:** Only work-item workflow skills listed above (not helpers like `speak`, not `command/` prompts, not the main agent loop).
- **Marker format:** Exactly `</end_session>` on its own line, as the final line of the final agent message.
- **Preserve existing output:** Skills still output their normal summary/AC/Effort-Risk content; `</end_session>` is an additional terminator, not a replacement.
- **Question-ended sessions:** If a skill session ends with unanswered questions for the operator, `</end_session>` is **not** emitted.

## Existing state

- Skills end sessions with ad-hoc closing text:
  - `skill/implement/SKILL.md`: "Close your response with: `<work-item-id>: <concise-summary>

Work committed to dev`"
  - `skill/intake/SKILL.md`: "Finish with 'This completes the Intake process for <work-item-id> <work-item-title>'"
  - `skill/plan/SKILL.md`: "End with: 'This completes the Plan process for <work-item-id>'"
- No skill currently outputs `</end_session>`.
- Related item SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S (standardize report format) is in `plan_complete` stage with 4 children; this intake is folded into that item's scope (per operator decision).

## Desired change

Add one instruction line to each work-item skill's SKILL.md final step: "End with `</end_session>`" (or equivalent phrasing that fits the skill's closing style). The `</end_session>` marker is appended after whatever closing summary the skill already produces.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to finishing step
- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to final report output
- `skill/cleanup/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/test/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/triage/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/code-review/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/resolve-pr-comments/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/effort-and-risk/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/find-related/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/author-command/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/report/SKILL.md` — ensure report helper emits `</end_session>` as final output line
- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — emits final `</end_session>` line when producing a report

> **Note:** `skill/git-management/SKILL.md` and `skill/owner-inference/SKILL.md` were listed in the original intake but were deleted in SA-0MSN81W9G006K0K8 (Retire owner-inference and git-management skills) — they are no longer in scope. Effective workflow-skill scope is now 14 files + the report helper (15).

## Related work

- **Standardize skill session end-of-session reporting via helper report skill (SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S)** — open / plan_complete / feature. This intake is folded into that item. Children: SA-0MSRFPUTN0089F3U, SA-0MSRFTP2Y008BH6L, SA-0MSRFTUGH002IZE4, SA-0MSRFTYOI000W0IQ. The report helper skill's children are in scope for adding `</end_session>` to their final outputs.
- **Skills: tag pi sessions spawned from skills with --session-id (SA-0MSNYWMJJ002CIJ7)** — open. Tangential — session tagging, not end markers.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep risk:** Updating 16 SKILL.md files is mechanical but broad; each needs individual review to ensure the marker line fits naturally into the existing closing convention. All work-item skills are explicitly listed — no new skills added mid-flight.
- **Coordination with SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S children:** The report helper skill's closing steps are defined by SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S's children; if those children are implemented before this work, their SKILL.md updates may need to include `</end_session>`. The children share this parent work item so coordination is internal to SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S.
- **Question-ended sessions:** Agents may occasionally forget to skip `</end_session>` when a question is pending. This is a soft risk — the marker is cosmetic; the real signal is workflow state.
- **Assumption:** The report helper skill (SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S children) will be wired into all work-item skills and should also emit `</end_session>` when it produces a report.
- **Assumption:** `speak` is the only helper-only skill excluded (no session lifecycle). If other helpers exist without sessions, they are also excluded.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Relationship to the report-format standardization item (SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S)?" — Answer (operator): "(c) folded into that item as an AC / the report helper should emit the marker too." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Scope of 'all skills'?" — Answer (operator): "(b) only work-item workflow skills — intake, plan, implement, audit, test, triage, ship, refactor, cleanup, effort-and-risk, find-related, code-review, resolve-pr-comments, git-management, owner-inference, author-command." Excludes helpers like `speak`. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Exact format & consumer?" — Answer (operator): "Exactly `</end_session>`, consumed by both humans and automation, only emitted on terminal state (no open questions)." Source: interactive reply.
data.title: All skills emit </end_session> marker on terminal state

# Retire owner-inference and git-management skills

## Problem statement

A review of all installed agent skills (session, priority medium) found that two skills should be removed: `owner-inference` (a code-only module with a single consumer) and `git-management` (a broken orphan that duplicates functionality already embedded in implement/ship/cleanup). Three helper skills (`effort-and-risk`, `triage`, `find-related`) were reviewed and intentionally **kept as-is** — no changes. `speak` is explicitly out of scope ("leave speak for now").

## Decisions (operator-confirmed)

1. **No changes** to effort-and-risk, triage, find-related — keep as shared code-only helpers (multi-caller, folding would duplicate code).
2. **Delete `owner-inference`** (do not fold into triage). It is a Python module (`infer_owner.py`) with a single consumer: triage's `check_or_create.py`. Triage will fall back to the deterministic `Build` assignee.
3. **Retire `git-management`** (option b). It is not referenced by any workflow skill (implement creates worktrees itself and uses ship's `pushToDev()`; ship owns branch naming/validation via `git-helpers.js`; cleanup owns pruning). Its `cleanup.mjs` action has a verified path bug in the installed symlink location (`~/.pi/agent/skill/` vs `~/.pi/agent/skills/`) — resolves `CLEANUP_SCRIPTS_DIR` to a non-existent path and exits "Cleanup infrastructure not found".

## Users

- **Pi agent operators** who maintain the installed skill set (`~/.pi/agent/skills` → this repo's `skill/`).
- **Agents** running triage on failing tests — test-failure issues will get assignee `Build` (fallback) instead of a git-heuristic owner.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `skill/owner-inference/` and `skill/owner_inference/` (compat shim package) are deleted from the repository
- [ ] `skill/git-management/` is deleted from the repository
- [ ] `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` skill-invocation map no longer references `owner-inference` or `git-management`
- [ ] `skill/triage/` no longer references owner-inference anywhere (`SKILL.md`, `scripts/check_or_create.py`, `resources/runbook-test-failure.md`, `resources/test-failure-template.md`); new test-failure issues deterministically use assignee `Build`
- [ ] `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` no longer references git-management
- [ ] All tests referencing deleted code are removed or updated (incl. `tests/test_skill_invocation_map.py`, `tests/test_infer_owner.py`, `tests/unit/test-owner-inference-skill.mjs`, `tests/unit/test-git-management-skill.mjs`, `tests/unit/test-git-mgmt-helpers*.mjs`, `tests/unit/test-merge-pr-worklog-gating.mjs`, `tests/integration/test-commit.mjs`, `tests/integration/test-create-branch.mjs`, `tests/integration/test-push.mjs`)
- [ ] No dangling references to the deleted skills remain anywhere in `skill/`, `docs/`, or `tests/` (grep-clean)
- [ ] Full project test suite passes (pytest + node suites)

## Constraints

- Changes are restricted to the deletion targets and their reference surface — do not modify the kept skills (`effort-and-risk`, `triage` behaviour beyond owner-inference removal, `find-related`, `speak`).
- `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded (managed by the ship skill's release pipeline).
- Follow the worktree workflow: all changes in the worktree created by `implement.py start <id>`; commit and push to `dev` per AGENTS.md.

## Key Files

- `skill/owner-inference/` — delete (SKILL.md + scripts/infer_owner.py)
- `skill/owner_inference/` — delete (compat shim package)
- `skill/git-management/` — delete (SKILL.md + 8 scripts)
- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` — remove rows: `owner-inference` (line ~104), `git-management` (line ~109)
- `skill/triage/scripts/check_or_create.py` — remove owner-inference import/integration (infer_owner fn ~142-158, call at ~451, owner_line at ~178)
- `skill/triage/SKILL.md` — remove owner-inference references (lines ~36, ~58)
- `skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md` — line ~68
- `skill/triage/resources/test-failure-template.md` — line ~36
- `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` — remove git-management rows (~265-272)
- `tests/test_skill_invocation_map.py` — remove both names from the expected list

## Related work

- Review session decisions recorded here; `speak` reviewed but explicitly deferred ("leave speak for now") — no change.

# Intake Brief: Always mark items as in_progress while an agent is working on them (SA-0MTFTFUIH000UWM9)

## Problem Statement

Agents must hold `status: in_progress` for the entire duration they are actively working on a work item. During the 2026-08-30 incident, a plan run released AH-0MTFPDKDU006QUDC to `open` at 12:08:51Z to pause for producer approval and never re-claimed after approval at 12:09:42Z, leaving the item `open` while creating children and updating descriptions until 12:18:40Z — allowing the herdr downtime worker to legitimately dispatch a duplicate `/skill:plan` at 12:13:02Z.

## Users

- **Operator** — wants the worklog to truthfully show whether an item is claimed, so downtime dispatch never duplicates work that is already in progress.
  - *Story:* As an operator, I want any active agent workflow to hold `in_progress` so `wl next` and the downtime worker do not re-dispatch the same item.
- **Agent (plan/intake/implement/audit/effort-and-risk)** — needs a clear, enforced lifecycle so pause/resume and error paths cannot silently leave an item `open` while mutations continue.
  - *Story:* As an agent running plan, after producer approval resumes my run I want the re-claim to be automatic/required before any child creation or description update.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Plan skill re-claims `status: in_progress` immediately after producer approval resumes a paused run, before any further work (child creation, dep wiring, description/comment updates); verified by a test driving the approval-gate flow where the item is `in_progress` continuously from approval through completion and never `open` in that window.
- [ ] No agent process performs work-item mutations (create children, update description, wire deps, completion comments) while `status: open`; SKILL.md files for plan, intake, implement, audit, and effort-and-risk are reviewed and updated to enforce claim-before-work and re-claim-after-any-pause, with any remaining `release to open while work continues` patterns eliminated or explicitly documented as handoff-only.
- [ ] A downtime-dispatched plan run that hits the approval gate with no interactive user does not release the item to `open` while the run remains active (holds claim or aborts cleanly).
- [ ] StatusLifecycle (shared helper) provides a mechanism to assert/automate re-claim on resume (e.g. `require_claimed` guard and/or `on_resume` re-claim), with unit tests covering the pause→approval→re-claim path and the guard failure when work is attempted on `open`.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes; `wl sync` is clean.

## Constraints

- Must not introduce orphaned `in_progress` items: every claim has a matching terminal release (`open`/`blocked`/`completed`) on completion, error/abort, or genuine session handoff.
- `completed` status remains compatible only with `in_review`/`done` stages (wl CLI validation); skills that restore on exit must not force `completed` on `idea`/`intake_complete`/`plan_complete`.
- Worklog-dir resolution must remain correct regardless of caller cwd (reuse `run_wl`/`resolve_worklog_flags`, prefix-to-sibling scan).
- Change is to agent framework (SorraAgents) — affects every project once installed via `scripts/install_pi.sh`; needs work-item tracking, tests, and push to `dev`.

## Existing State

- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` line 42 specifies claim-first via `StatusLifecycle.update_status(<id>, "in_progress")` and line 47 specifies "Pausing for producer input" → `update_status(<id>, "open", needs_producer_review=True)`. The manual run at 2026-08-30T12:08:51Z followed the pause-release but never re-claimed after approval at 12:09:42Z before creating 3 children at 12:11:28Z.
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` provides `StatusLifecycle` context manager and `update_status`/`show`/`run_wl` helpers with worklog-dir injection; no `require_claimed` guard or resume re-claim helper exists yet.
- Other skills (intake, implement, audit, effort-and-risk) have varying lifecycle adherence; previous migrations (SA-0MS69FE4Q008N8SZ, SA-0MS1MQ8GF002YXZO) wired StatusLifecycle into some skills but not uniformly.
- Downtime worker dispatches `critical + open + intake_complete` candidates via CAS (`--if-status open --if-stage intake_complete`), so any `open` window during active work is a duplicate-dispatch hazard.

## Desired Change

- Enforce invariant: **actively worked => `in_progress`; released to `open` only at true handoff** (completion, error/abort, or session actually ending).
- Plan skill: after producer approval, immediately re-claim `in_progress` before any work-bearing step; add a guard that the item is `in_progress` before child creation/dep wiring/description updates.
- SKILL.md guidance: clarify that pause-release applies only when the session hands control back for an open-ended wait with no in-session resume; approval-resume must re-claim.
- Shared helper: add `require_claimed(id)` and/or `on_resume` re-claim flow used by skills before mutations.
- Downtime plan runs hitting the approval gate hold the claim (keep `in_progress`) or abort cleanly — never release to `open` mid-run.

## Key Files

- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — Clarify pause vs. handoff semantics; require re-claim after approval before any work.
- `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` — Approval-gate and plan-if-needed helpers; ensure they re-claim or hold claim.
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — Add `require_claimed` guard and/or resume re-claim helper; add tests.
- `skill/shared/test_status_lifecycle.py` — Extend with pause→approval→re-claim and guard tests.
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — Verify claim-before-work and re-claim-after-pause compliance.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — Verify claim-before-work compliance.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — Verify claim-before-work compliance.
- `skill/effort-and-risk/SKILL.md` — Verify restore_on_exit vs. claim semantics.
- `README.md` — Agent Status Lifecycle section documenting the in_progress invariant (SA-0MTFTFUIH000UWM9).

## Related Work

- Potentially related work items:
  - SA-0MS69FE4Q008N8SZ — Implement and plan skills don't use StatusLifecycle context manager (completed)
  - SA-0MS1MQ8GF002YXZO — Wire shared StatusLifecycle into implementall, intakeall, planall (completed)
  - SA-0MS93J0ZC007IO8V — Skill scripts rely on caller cwd for wl and force status=completed (completed)
  - SA-0MS31SAM20004GTJ — All actions should leave the status in a good state (completed)
  - SA-0MTG0Y34T007ZHPF — When multiple agents are working they can become blocked on audits/testing (in_progress) — related downtime/idle-gate interaction
  - SA-0MTFTFUIH000UWM9 — This item (root cause: AH-0MTFPDKDU006QUDC at 2026-08-30T12:13:02.827Z duplicate dispatch; manual plan session 2026-08-30T12-03-10-333Z)
- Potentially related docs:
  - `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — Shared lifecycle helper (source of invariant enforcement)
  - `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — Plan skill claim/pause lifecycle (lines 42, 47, 112)
  - `docs/dev/plan-skill-reference.md` — Plan implementation reference
  - `docs/dev/intake-skill-reference.md` — Intake reference (worklog resolution, issue type guide)
  - `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` — Worklog sync and worklog-dir resolution

## Risks & Assumptions

- Risk: Over-eager re-claim could mask genuine handoffs and leave items stuck `in_progress` visible as orphaned. Mitigation: re-claim only on in-session resume; terminal release still required on completion/error/abort.
- Risk: `wl` CAS dispatch relies on `open` to find candidates; holding `in_progress` longer reduces dispatch surface but may starve other work if claim is held too long. Mitigation: scope claim to actual work duration; no change to dispatch query.
- Risk: Existing skills without StatusLifecycle coverage may regress. Mitigation: audit all five skills and add guards/tests.
- Assumption: Producer approval in interactive pane is in-session resume (not handoff) — validated by incident timeline.
- Assumption: Downtime worker has no interactive approver; holding claim is preferred to releasing to `open`. Needs validation with herdr/downtime code.
- Scope-creep risk: Generalizing to a repo-wide status invariant could expand to queue/dispatch policy changes — record as linked follow-ups, not in-scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Who is the primary user for this invariant?" — Answer (inferred from description): Operator and agent workflows; operator wants truthful claimed state, agents need enforced lifecycle. Source: work item description Goals/user story. No new interview needed — brief is well-defined.
- Q: "Should downtime-dispatched runs ever release to open mid-run?" — Answer (from description): No — hold claim or abort cleanly. Source: description Required behaviour #4 and Suggested implementation. OPEN QUESTION retained for herdr/downtime implementation detail: confirm preferred abort vs. hold behavior with herdr maintainer if code path differs.
- Q: "Does this duplicate SA-0MS69FE4Q008N8SZ / SA-0MS1MQ8GF002YXZO?" — Answer: No — those wired StatusLifecycle into skills; this item fixes the pause→resume re-claim gap those did not cover (incident at 12:08:51Z–12:11:28Z). Source: wl search and description root cause recap. Research: searched work items for StatusLifecycle/plan skill; prior items completed without resume guard.
